web_title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan
book_title: Chapter 9: Bull vs. Bear, Likely Outcomes & Our Action Plan
question: Weighing the strongest Bull and Bear arguments against our price-blind business audit, ex-SBC valuation, and Stage 1/Stage 4 tape, what is our independent verdict across all three horizons, our current holding action, and our capital redeployment plan?

epigraph.quote: The stock market is a no-called-strike game. You don't have to swing at everything—you can wait for your pitch.
epigraph.author: Warren Buffett

web_blocks.title: 9.1 Steelmanning Both Sides of the Aisle: Bull vs. Bear

web_blocks.html: Sound investing starts by stating the strongest honest case for both bulls and bears before picking a side. In Cirrus Logic's case, the debate pits a debt-free, high-ROIC engineering franchise against 93% single-customer risk and shrinking near-term sales. The side-by-side matrix below weighs both arguments against audited filings and live market data [1][2][27].

web_blocks.caption: Cirrus Logic (CRUS): Unbiased Bull vs. Bear Evidence Matrix
rows: Deep 15+ year co-engineering bond with Apple across 22nm codecs, boosted amps, haptics, and camera controllers; 4,340 patents create switching friction [1][2].
Apple rose from 79% (FY17) to 91% (FY26) and 93% (Q2 FY27); Dialog and Imagination prove Apple in-houses key silicon when strategic [1][2][20][22].
Moat is real inside current sockets, but 93% single-buyer reliance creates permanent binary risk that caps the multiple.
HPMS grew +11.1% YoY in H1 FY27 to 44.7% of sales; SoundWire chips won slots at top 5–6 laptop OEMs, and INVENTVM adds edge reach [2][3][7][15].
9-year sales CAGR is 2.9%; Lion ($335M) took an $85.8M write-down; 2026–2027 PC memory shortages delay launches; Q3 guide is -7% YoY [1][3][10].
Diversification is encouraging, yet too small (~7% non-Apple in Q2 FY27) to move total sales before FY2028.
52.8%–53.7% GAAP GM, $1,076.43M net cash ($0 debt), 34.7% op. ROIC, $1.67B in 10-year buybacks (2.56x SBC), new $500M plan [1][2][3].
Q2 GM had a one-off GlobalFoundries credit; Q3 GM guides to 51%–53%; FY26 FCF had ~$102M WC release; new $600M GF wafer deal adds fixed risk [1][2][3].
The balance sheet is a fortress ($20.91/sh cash), but steady ex-SBC FCF is ~$430M—not $637M—and buybacks alone cannot re-rate the stock.
Trades at 14.61x P/E and 10.03x EV/EBITDA (27% below 10Y P/E mean of 20.06x); held up better than analog peers on Nov 24 [27][28][29].
Ex-SBC Base FV is $126.00 (+8.9%); price sits -12.53% below 30W SMA ($132.30) and -15.91% below 200D SMA ($137.61) in a Downtrend [28][41].
Fairly priced for 2%–3% growth; fails both our >=1.50:1 risk-reward hurdle (0.69:1–0.92:1) and our Stage 2 trend gate.
web_blocks.takeaway: CRUS is a cash-rich niche franchise, not a broken firm. Yet 93% customer reliance, -7% Q3 guidance, thin 8.9% upside, and a broken chart leave zero edge.

web_blocks.html: Our probability-weighted 12-month expected value lands at **$124.25** ($124.42 exact). That is just **+7.4%** above the November 24 close of $115.72, trailing our 10.8% cost of equity by 340 bps. The risk-reward math is just as clear. A real structural stop at **$104.50** (below the $105.10 52-week low, 2.62x ATR) puts $12.75 at risk from the $117.25 zone high against $8.75 of upside to $126.00. That yields **0.69:1** R:R (**0.92:1** from CMP $115.72). Waiting for a Stage 2 breakout above the 30-week SMA ($132.30) means paying 5.0% *above* Base value. Neither entry clears our 1.50:1 bar, so we do not hedge with `WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT`. Our verdict is **`REJECTED`** on **`VALUATION`** and **`TREND`**.

web_blocks.caption: Cirrus Logic (CRUS): 12-Month Probability-Weighted Scenario Matrix (CMP: $115.72)
rows: Apple socket or margin pressure cuts ex-SBC FCF -5% per year; net cash ($20.91/sh) cushions the floor.
FY27–FY28 sales hold near $1.95B–$2.10B (+3% FCF growth); Apple stays ~90%; gross margin settles at 51%–52%.
Windows AI PC SoundWire + HPMS wins lift non-Apple share past 15% and drive +7% FCF growth at 18x–19x P/E.
Expected return (+7.4%) trails 10.8% cost of equity; support R:R (0.69:1) misses the 1.50:1 hurdle.
web_blocks.takeaway: Probability-weighted return (+7.4%) does not pay for 93% single-customer risk when 10-year Treasuries yield 4.92%.

web_blocks.title: 9.3 Multi-Horizon Investment Judgment (Short / Medium / Long Term)

web_blocks.html: A single stock can look very different to a short-term swing trader, a medium-term inflection buyer, and a multi-year compounder. Separating these three horizons prevents mixing a broken chart with a long-term thesis. The table below states our independent verdict and exact reversal trigger for each time horizon [28][41].

web_blocks.caption: Cirrus Logic (CRUS): Three-Horizon Independent Verdict
rows: Sits -12.53% below 30W SMA ($132.30) and -15.91% below 200D SMA ($137.61) in a Downtrend with 2.0% chip 50D breadth; options are illiquid [28][41].
Q3 FY27 guidance ($540M, -7% YoY) and PC memory delays push non-Apple ramps to FY2028; 0.69:1–0.92:1 R:R fails our 1.50:1 bar [3][28].
CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL quality: 34.7% op. ROIC and $1.08B cash are capped by 93% Apple share and 2.9% 9Y CAGR. Revisit if non-Apple >20% [1][2].
web_blocks.takeaway: No horizon clears our bar today: momentum is broken, near-term sales are shrinking, and long-term compounding is capped by 93% Apple reliance.

web_blocks.title: 9.4 Current Holding Action, Advisory Alerts & 100% Capital Redeployment Plan

web_blocks.html: Per the November 24, 2026 positions ledger (`positions_US_2026-11-24.json`), **CRUS is NOT HELD** at Schwab or Robinhood (0 shares, $0.00 value) [41]. Our `holding_action` is **`NOT_HELD`** with **0 shares to sell**. No broker orders are needed. Instead, we set two clear advisory alerts. First, a **Deep Value Washout Gate** triggers if CRUS drops to $95.00–$100.00 (near Pivot S2 $94.74) with intact Apple sockets and >=51% gross margins. Second, a **Stage 2 Inflection Gate** triggers if non-Apple sales pass 15%–20%, revenue growth clears >8% YoY, and price reclaims the 30-week SMA ($132.30) on strong volume.

Because no CRUS shares are sold, the capital under review is our next marginal USD unit from **$7,290.91 in consolidated cash** ($4,772.99 Schwab + $2,517.92 Robinhood) [41]. That cash is just **8.73%** of our $83,506.98 US net worth [41]. The S&P 500 is in a 10-distribution-day **Downtrend** (27.8% >50-DMA), and our portfolio already carries **225.3% beta-weighted S&P 500 exposure** ($188,182.45 across 17 active positions, including five chip stocks: QCOM, TXN, ASX, SKHY, and TSM) [41]. Adding a broken-trend chipmaker would compound macro risk. We allocate **100.0% to CASH**, **0.0% to shortlist ETF XLV**, and **0.0% to outside peer SLAB**.

Decision Reversal Trigger: Re-underwrite CRUS only if (1) price washes out to $95.00–$100.00 with >=51% GM and intact Apple sockets (creating >=1.50:1 R:R to $126.00 Base value), OR (2) non-Apple revenue exceeds 15%–20% with >8% YoY growth and a high-volume weekly close above the 30-week SMA ($132.30).

book_paragraphs: We have walked through forty years of Cirrus Logic's history, dissected every silicon socket inside a flagship smartphone and an AI laptop, audited ten years of SEC filings, built a clean ex-SBC cash-flow model, and inspected the price chart across three timeframes. Now comes the moment that separates institutional discipline from storytelling: putting both sides of the aisle on the scale and making a clean, unhedged call.

First, let us give the Bull case its absolute strongest voice. Cirrus Logic is not a low-quality business. It is an engineering powerhouse with 4,340 issued and pending patents, a 15-year co-design partnership with the most demanding hardware company on earth, 52.8% to 53.7% GAAP gross margins, 34.7% operating ROIC, and $1.08 billion in cash with zero funded debt. Management has returned $1.67 billion via buybacks over the last decade—covering stock-based compensation 2.56 times over and shrinking the diluted share count by more than 20%. At 14.61x earnings and 10.03x EV/EBITDA, you are paying a 27% discount to Cirrus Logic's ten-year average P/E for a company that just beat Q2 FY2027 adjusted EPS estimates by 11.5% and is quietly expanding its High-Performance Mixed-Signal franchise and Windows AI PC SoundWire footprint.

Now let us give the Bear case equal weight, without flinching. Every dollar of that high-margin profitability sits on a single pillar that has grown narrower, not wider: Apple accounted for 79% of revenue in FY2017, 89% in FY2025, 91% in FY2026, and an astonishing 93% in Q2 FY2027. History is brutal to suppliers with 80%+ Apple concentration—Dialog Semiconductor lost its flagship PMIC sockets and was forced into a $600 million IP/engineer transfer, and Imagination Technologies lost 70% of its market value in a single morning. Meanwhile, Cirrus Logic's nine-year revenue CAGR is just 2.9%, the $335 million Lion Semiconductor acquisition suffered an $85.8 million impairment, Q3 FY2027 revenue guidance just stepped down to -7% year-over-year at the midpoint, and 2026–2027 PC memory shortages are delaying the very laptop ramps bulls need to diversify away from handsets.

When we weigh both sides numerically, the verdict writes itself. Our probability-weighted 12-month expected value—25% Bear at $84.50, 50% Base at $126.00, and 25% Bull at $160.50—lands at $124.25 per share. That is a +7.4% expected return, which sits 340 basis points *below* Cirrus Logic's 10.8% cost of equity. Worse, test the trade mechanics with an honest structural stop. Placing a stop below the $105.10 52-week low at $104.50 risks $11.22 from today's $115.72 price (or $12.75 from the $117.25 support-zone high) to reach a $126.00 Base target—a reward-to-risk ratio of just 0.69:1 to 0.92:1. And if you wait for a confirmed Stage 2 breakout above the 30-week moving average at $132.30, you would be buying the stock 5% *above* our Base intrinsic value. There is no honest entry price on today's chart that clears our 1.50:1 asymmetry hurdle.

That is why we refuse to hide behind a timid 'Wait for Support' label. Our new-capital verdict is REJECTED on Valuation and Trend. Across all three horizons, the answer is consistent: short-term momentum traders have no edge beneath a falling 30-week SMA in a 2%-breadth semiconductor tape with illiquid options; medium-term inflection investors face a -7% YoY Q3 revenue air pocket and delayed PC launches; and long-term compounders cannot ignore 93% single-customer concentration with 2.9% nine-year top-line growth.

Finally, let us connect this decision directly to our live U.S. portfolio. Per the November 24, 2026 positions ledger, we hold zero shares of Cirrus Logic across Charles Schwab and Robinhood, so our holding action is NOT_HELD with zero shares to sell. Looking at our next marginal dollar of capital from our $7,290.91 consolidated cash reserve (just 8.73% of our $83,506.98 net worth), our portfolio already carries 225.3% beta-weighted effective S&P 500 exposure—including five existing semiconductor names—inside a 10-distribution-day market Downtrend. We evaluated our best Stage 2 active shortlist candidate, the Healthcare Sector ETF (XLV at $184.72), and the only Stage 2 peer in Cirrus Logic's analog group, Silicon Laboratories (SLAB at $220.91, excluded on negative ROIC and negative upside to consensus). Neither justifies draining our scarce cash buffer right now. We keep 100% of marginal capital in USD cash earning nearly 5% risk-free, set our advisory alerts for either a deep value washout below $100 or a genuine non-Apple fundamental inflection above the 30-week SMA, and move cleanly to the next opportunity.

What would make you and me change our minds? Good research never ends with a permanent grudge; it ends with falsifiable, objective milestones. First, on the deep-value side, if a broad market washout drags CRUS down into the $95.00 to $100.00 zone—near Pivot S2 at $94.74—while Apple socket retention holds intact and GAAP gross margins stay above 51%, then the $20.91 per share net-cash cushion would represent more than 21% of the stock price and upside to our $126.00 Base value would widen past 26%, finally restoring an asymmetric margin of safety. Second, on the fundamental-growth side, if Cirrus Logic's Windows AI PC SoundWire codecs and INVENTVM-enhanced HPMS portfolio push non-Apple revenue above 15% to 20% of sales, restore consolidated top-line growth above 8% year-over-year, and drive a high-volume weekly reclaim above the 30-week moving average ($132.30), our Base intrinsic value would step up materially and warrant a fresh re-underwriting. Until one of those two concrete gates triggers, discipline demands keeping CRUS on the rejected bench and protecting our 8.73% USD cash reserve.

book_callouts.title: Narrator's Reflection: Passing on a Good Company Is a Winning Decision
book_callouts.text: One of the hardest lessons in institutional investing is that a profitable, debt-free, well-run company can still be a clean REJECT. Cirrus Logic is not going bankrupt tomorrow; its $1.08 billion cash pile and Apple engineering bond ensure survival. But your job is not to collect 'nice' companies—your job is to deploy scarce capital only when business quality, valuation asymmetry (>=1.50:1), and Stage 2 institutional sponsorship align. Today, CRUS gives you zero of those three in full measure. Saying 'no' preserves your cash for the pitch that actually clears the fence.
